text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Iran and Pakistan called on the warring factions in neighbouring Afghanistan to lay down their arms and search for a settlement through negotiations.

- Business activities in Karachi were crippled as major business centres and markets in several parts of the city remained closed amid tension after the massacre on Monday of five workers of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
- An official U.S. delegation is arriving in Islamabad in a couple of days to sort out some of the major irritants between the two countries in the area of narcotics control.
- Water and Power Minister Nisar Ali Khan said a new policy for private power generation would be announced by mid-July.
- The Indian army chief accused Pakistan of placing missiles on its border and denied India had done the same, the Press Trust of India reported.
- Gunmen killed a Shi'ite activist in the latest incident in a wave of sectarian violence, police said.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange suspended membership of broking firm M. Rashid Jamal for defaults of over 100 million rupees.
- The International Monetary Fund is likely to enter talks with Pakistan for a three-year, $1.5-billion extended structural adjustment facility by the end of July, sources said.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan cut the discount or repo rate by one percent to 19 percent.
- The Law and Justice Ministry has advised the Privatisation Commission to repossess Naya Daur Motors Ltd if the company that bought it from the government fails to pay the full amount.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- A holding company will be created to facilitate privatisation of state-run petroleum companies, sources said.
- White sugar imports have created a glut in the local market, but prices have not fallen to a reasonable level.
- The government will announce a comprehensive reform package for insurance companies which will include establishment of an independent insurance regulatory authority.
- Al-Baraka Samah Group is reported to have concluded an agreement to buy the private Platinum Bank from the local Chakwal Group.
- The Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry has asked the government to cut what it calls high tax rates on banking companies to help bring down corporate lending rates.
THE NEWS
- Former chief secretary Punjab Aslam Hayyat Qureshi has been arrested by the Federal Investigation Agency for alleged involvement in a rice deal scandal.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz will brief envoys of the Aid-to-Pakistan consortium on the proposed budget for 1997/98 (July-June).
- The government has withdrawn a concessional general sales tax slab of 10 percent on export and imposed a uniform rate of 12.5 percent across the board.
THE MUSLIM

- The government has finalised a corruption case against Asif Ali Zardari, spouse of opposition leader Benazir Bhutto, on charges related to the construction of a polo ground at the prime minister's house.
THE NATION
- Indian Foreign Secretary Salman Haider arrives on Thursday for a second round of talks with his Pakistani counterpart.
